decontamination_notes: Real bug fix from spf13/pflag PR #487, merged 2026-07-02. Labeled decontaminated: true because the fix post-dates the May 2026 training cutoff of the models this suite targets (Claude Opus 5); re-check `upstream_merged` against any newer model's cutoff before reusing. pflag decided whether a flag was boolean-like by type-asserting its Value to the unexported boolFlag interface without ever calling IsBoolFlag(), and only auto-assigned NoOptDefVal="true" when Value.Type() was literally "bool". A custom Value returning true from IsBoolFlag() but reporting another Type() therefore never got NoOptDefVal and failed to parse without an argument ('flag needs an argument'), while a Value returning false from IsBoolFlag() was still treated as bool-like in some paths. The fix adds isNoOptBoolValue() in bool.go and routes the checks in flag.go through it. Repo sliced at the PR base commit (6404d820); pflag is a zero-dependency module (go.mod declares only the module path and go 1.12), so no vendoring is needed and the base sandbox image suffices. The repo's own *_test.go files at the module root are removed from the slice. Coverage: 3 fail_to_pass tests, each verified to fail at the base commit and pass after the gold patch, covering NoOptDefVal assignment, parsing with no argument, and a following operand remaining a positional arg rather than being consumed. The 4 pass_to_pass guards live in a SEPARATE package (osscheck_reg) per the v3 Go recipe and cover a built-in bool flag, a built-in string flag still requiring an argument, a plain custom Value with no IsBoolFlag() method, and an explicit inline --verbose=false. NOTE: a fourth candidate f2p test asserting that --verbose=false is honored was written and observed to PASS at the base commit -- supplying the value inline never depended on NoOptDefVal -- so it was moved into the regression guard rather than counted as fail_to_pass. All assertions go through the public pflag API (NewFlagSet, Var, Lookup, Parse, Args).
